A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and can be matched reliably despite reflow and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original pretraining experiments, nine-benchmark evaluations and controlled generation results in Section 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds measurements of attention to metadata components across model layers.

M1.justification: Both versions use metadata loss masking, uniformly mixed 90% conditioned and 10% context-free pretraining, and the same classifier-free guidance procedure. The added attention analysis examines existing checkpoints without changing the method.

E1.justification: FineWeb-Edu, the nine downstream benchmarks, health/history continuation tasks and steering scenarios are retained. The new attention study samples the existing training corpus without introducing another domain or task.

E2.justification: MeCo is newly included in Figure 3's training-perplexity comparison, although it already appeared in v1's downstream comparisons in Tables 1–2. Other comparator memberships remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix C.1.2 introduces an attention-analysis protocol using 100 randomly sampled documents, batch size 1, sequence length 4096, no padding, and attention aggregation and normalization. Existing pretraining and downstream evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds a focused diagnostic study of attention to different metadata components and its evolution across layers, shown in Figures 5 and 8. Existing metadata controls, guidance-factor sensitivity analysis and steering examples are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report three-seed LLM-judge evaluation with means and standard deviations, including the guidance-factor plot. The new attention measurements introduce no additional repeated-run, uncertainty or significance reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 and the generation examples retain their results. v2 adds attention findings, including URL-prefix attention concentration from layer 3, and a MeCo perplexity curve. Figure 3's left panel also revises the URL and DI traces, with DI displayed over a shorter training interval; the PDFs do not establish a changed training budget.

T1.justification: The sampling expressions, guidance equation and interpretations of the guidance parameter are retained. Neither version supplies theoretical results or proofs, and the new attention analysis adds no formal theoretical development.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same scientific claims: URL metadata accelerates pretraining, downstream gains depend on longer prompts, and topic/format metadata enables interpretable steering.

C2.justification: v2 proposes that early-layer attention to meaningful URL components helps explain training acceleration, interprets later prefix concentration as an attention sink, and discusses URLs' implicit quality/domain information. These extend v1's unresolved mechanism discussion; Appendix A's scale and corpus limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-access link in the abstract and documents attention extraction, averaging and normalization. Existing training details, hardware costs and judge prompts are retained. Code availability is described inconsistently: the new checklist still says the code will be released later.

R1.justification: The same 25 research references and substantive positioning against metadata-conditioning and generation-guidance research are retained. Naming Higuchi et al. beside an existing citation does not change the relationship to prior work.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence remain intact. v2 adds the 'Why only URL helps?' discussion, subdivides Appendix C.1, inserts a NeurIPS checklist, and updates front matter and acknowledgments.

P2.justification: v2 adds attention bar charts and a heatmap in Figures 5 and 8, and revises Figure 3's plotted series and legend. Existing displays are otherwise retained with figure renumbering, relocation and document reflow.

improvement.justification: The documented attention study adds useful observational evidence about a mechanism that v1 left unresolved, while the MeCo curve makes the training comparison more complete. These are limited gains: the mechanism remains hypothetical, principal benchmark results and generalization limits are unchanged, and code-access statements conflict. Overall, v2 modestly improves explanation and documentation.
